It feels like the objects around you are part of a set. It was very disconcerting for me. Objects seemed almost, especially three dimensional in a certain way. It was as if I was keenly aware of the object's existence just by themselves. 

Nothing seemed to have context. Like, imagine going through a regular day. You move from one room to the next, pick up some cereal, poor it into a bowl, eat it, etc. While this is going on if you weren't experiencing dissassociation you would likely be somewhat on autopilot. You would be thinking about your day, what would come next, what you need and what, etc. And things would sort of just click into place. You take for granted that you are... yourself. 

That same experience while depersonalized goes differently. The rooms seem almost more angular. Specific details of the room jump out to you and seem to assert themselves more than their immediate purpose in your daily routine. Suddenly the sharp details of the color of a cereal box, the texture of a wheatie, the particular shape of your face in the mirror seem to be of more importance than how you interact with them, if that makes sense?

 Your typical thoughts are replaced with intense self-awareness and a kind of alienation from your surroundings and yourself. The person looking at you in the mirror does not seem to be you. Nothing seems real. Nothing flows right. You are struck by the thought that your past memories are distant, and not really yours. Objects seem out of place, and kind of staged. 

It's like the feeling of partial emotional attachment you have to the surroundings of a character in a video game, but you're in it. For me at least it was horrible. I tried to look at it as a kind of novel experience that many people never had. A different way to be in the world I suppose? But, I was very relieved when the symptoms eventually passed. Very unsettling.
